proposals.note: Proposed a highly expressive block using a ring topology (CNOTs connecting 0-1-2-3-4-5-0) to maximize connectivity and entanglement across all 6 qubits, addressing the limitation of linear topologies in prior proposals. The block structure follows a standard EfficientSU2-like pattern (RY layer, Entangler, RX layer, Entangler) with 12 trainable parameters. This design balances expressivity with trainability, avoiding the high parameter count of c0001/c0003 while ensuring full graph connectivity unlike the linear chains in c0002/c0004. The ring topology is suitable for the cyclic nature of the input indices [0..5].

proposals.note: Designed a highly symmetric ansatz block inspired by the low-risk c0005 structure. The block consists of two entangling layers (cyclic CNOT ladder) separated by uniform single-qubit rotations (RX and RY). Crucially, all RX gates share parameter 'p0' and all RY gates share 'p1'. This tied-parameter structure enforces translation invariance across the 6 sites, satisfying the hypothesis that the block is invariant under the cyclic permutation (0 1 2 3 4 5). This symmetry acts as a strong regularizer, reducing the effective parameter count to 2 while maintaining sufficient entanglement depth. The data re-uploading feature map provides the necessary non-linear input dependence, allowing this symmetric block to model the regression targets effectively while minimizing overfitting risk.

proposals.note: Adopted the structure of the best-performing prior proposal (c0005) which achieved the lowest development risk (0.0098). The block consists of two layers of a cyclic CNOT ladder (entanglement) followed by individual single-qubit rotations (RX then RY). This structure provides strong expressivity for the 6-site input while maintaining a simple, regular topology that is robust to optimization. No symmetry hypothesis is claimed, as the verifier report indicated that previous symmetry claims were invalid due to high residuals and label violations, suggesting the underlying task may not possess simple permutation invariance or the previous ansatz failed to realize it.

proposals.note: Design inspired by c0007 (lowest dev risk) but with a cyclic topology and tied parameters to enforce translation invariance. The block consists of two identical layers of RY rotations followed by a ring of CNOTs. Parameters are tied within each layer (ry0..ry5) and across layers, reducing parameter count to 6. The cyclic CNOT structure (0-1-2-3-4-5-0) combined with uniform RY parameters makes the ansatz block invariant under cyclic permutations of the qubits. This matches the likely structure of the input data (indexed sites) and the readout observables (Z_i, Z_iZ_j), allowing the model to generalize better by sharing weights across symmetric sites. The hypothesis claims invariance under the cyclic shift generator [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0].

This block uses a uniform rotation layer (tied parameters) followed by a cyclic nearest-neighbor entanglement layer (CNOTs 0-1, 1-2, ..., 5-0). This structure is equivariant under cyclic permutations of the qubits, satisfying the hypothesis. The parameter tying reduces the search space, while the cyclic entanglement captures local correlations consistent with the site-indexed input structure.

proposals.note: Adopted the structure from c0008 (lowest dev risk) which uses a cyclic CNOT topology and repeated RY layers. Added a rotational symmetry hypothesis (generator [1,2,3,4,5,0]) because the block structure is invariant under cyclic permutation of wires if parameters are permuted accordingly. This symmetry aligns with the likely periodic nature of the input data (angles) and the cyclic connectivity, potentially improving generalization and reducing overfitting by enforcing equivariance/invariance constraints.

proposals.note: Proposing a translation-invariant ansatz (cyclic shift symmetry) to match the periodic nature of the input domain [0, 2pi). The block consists of two layers of uniform RY rotations (tied parameters p0, p1) interleaved with a ring of CNOT gates. This structure is equivariant under cyclic permutations of the qubits. The hypothesis claims invariance under the cyclic group C6 generated by the shift (0->1->...->5->0). This reduces the parameter space significantly (2 params) and enforces a structural bias that aligns with the periodicity of the data, potentially improving generalization for regression targets derived from trigonometric functions.
